title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 11th District
area: Most of Morris County plus parts of Essex, Passaic, and Sussex counties, including Parsippany, Montclair, West Orange, Denville, and Wayne.

context.text: The seat became vacant when Rep. Mikie Sherrill (D) resigned after being elected Governor of New Jersey in November 2025. A special election was held to fill the remainder of her term: Analilia Mejia won the February 5, 2026 Democratic primary, then defeated Joe Hathaway (R) and Alan Bond (independent) in the special general election on April 16, 2026, and was sworn in on April 20, 2026.

Mejia is now running for a full two-year term. She defeated three challengers in the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary; Joe Hathaway again advanced unopposed as the Republican nominee. Alan Bond (Hope for Tomorrow Party) and write-in candidate Vincent Matrisciano (Common Sense Independent Party) are also on the November 3 general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Analilia Mejia
candidates.ballotNote: Won the April 16, 2026 special election and the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary

summary.text: Analilia Mejia is the Democratic incumbent for New Jersey's 11th Congressional District, elected in an April 2026 special election to succeed Mikie Sherrill after Sherrill became governor. She holds master's degrees in public affairs and labor relations from Rutgers University and spent about 25 years as a labor organizer, including as director of the New Jersey Working Families Alliance, deputy director of the U.S. Department of Labor's Women's Bureau, and national political director for Sen. Bernie Sanders' 2020 presidential campaign.

background.text: Earned master's degrees in public affairs and labor relations from Rutgers University in 2003.
Served as a union organizer and as director of the New Jersey Working Families Alliance.
Served as deputy director of the Women's Bureau at the U.S. Department of Labor.
Served as national political director for Sen. Bernie Sanders' 2020 presidential campaign, and co-director of the advocacy group Popular Democracy.

Won the special Democratic primary on February 5, 2026 with 29.3% in an 11-candidate field, then defeated Joe Hathaway (R) and Alan Bond (independent) in the April 16, 2026 special general election, taking 60.2% of the vote.

priorities.text: Making paid sick leave federal law, citing her role helping win paid sick days for hundreds of thousands of New Jersey workers.
priorities.quote: In Congress, I’ll make paid sick leave federal law so every worker can care for themselves and their family. No exceptions.

priorities.text: Expanding federal child-care subsidies by reintroducing a version of Mikie Sherrill's Child Care for Every Community Act, capping child-care costs at $10/day and no more than 7% of family income.
priorities.quote: In Congress, I’ll re-introduce Mikie Sherrill’s Child Care for Every Community Act in the House — ensuring families pay no more than $10 a day, lower-income families pay nothing, and no family pays more than 7% of their income on childcare.

priorities.text: Raising the federal minimum wage to $25/hour and exempting the first $40,000 of a full-time worker's wages from federal income tax.
Restoring federal funding for the Gateway Tunnel rail project and increasing federal funding for NJ Transit.
Passing Medicare for All, describing it as needed after what she calls Republican-driven cuts to health-insurance subsidies.

positions.summary: Supports a Medicare for All system with universal coverage, no out-of-pocket costs, and comprehensive benefits including dental, vision, and mental health care.
Supports raising the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour, citing her prior role leading the campaign that won a $15 state minimum wage in New Jersey.
Supports an Ultra-Millionaires' Tax on fortunes over $50 million, a minimum 25% income tax on billionaires including unrealized gains, and taxing investment income at the same rate as wages.
Supports the Homes for All Act to build 8.5 million public-housing units and a ban on hedge funds and private-equity firms buying single-family homes.
Supports a moratorium on new AI data centers and requiring big technology companies to pay for the energy they use, with proceeds invested in clean energy.

Supports capping child-care costs at $10 a day for families (free for lower-income families) by reintroducing the Child Care for Every Community Act and funding it with new taxes on billionaires and corporations.

record.text: Assumed office April 20, 2026 after winning the special election; the district's key House floor votes for the current Congress are compiled separately in this guide.

candidates.name: Joe Hathaway
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary unopposed; also the Republican nominee in the April 2026 special election, which he lost

summary.text: Joe Hathaway is the Republican nominee for New Jersey's 11th Congressional District. He is a former mayor of Randolph Township and Randolph Township Council member who also worked as an aide to Gov. Chris Christie, and lost the April 2026 special election to Analilia Mejia before winning the regular June 2026 primary unopposed.

background.text: Born in Clifton, New Jersey; earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Yale University in 2009.
Worked in healthcare and financial-sector executive communications and operations roles.
Served as an aide to New Jersey Gov. Chris Christie (R).
Served on the Randolph Township Council and as Mayor of Randolph.
Won the special Republican primary for NJ-11 in February 2026 with 97.4% of the vote, then lost the April 16, 2026 special general election to Analilia Mejia, 60.2%-39.4%.

priorities.text: Eliminating or freezing federal taxes for first-time homebuyers and creating a refundable federal tax credit to offset closing costs.
priorities.quote: I will support and introduce legislation that provides a federal tax freeze for first-time homebuyers during their first years of ownership, putting money back in the pockets of families when they need it most.

priorities.text: Pursuing an "all-of-the-above" energy strategy including nuclear, natural gas, solar, and land-based wind, while opposing offshore wind turbines off the Jersey Shore.
priorities.quote: I will not support policies that build offshore wind turbines or provide foreign companies with billion-dollar contracts.

priorities.text: Cutting federal regulations and red tape for small businesses and expanding tax incentives for local job creators.
Increasing funding and support for local law enforcement and border security, including anti-fentanyl trafficking enforcement.

positions.summary: Opposes offshore wind development off the New Jersey coast and supports continued production of natural gas and other fossil fuels alongside nuclear and land-based renewables.
Supports increased funding for Border Patrol technology and presence and stronger enforcement against fentanyl trafficking.
Supports securing federal funding for local police training, equipment, and technology.
Says he will stand firmly with Israel as it "combats terrorism" and with Ukraine against Russia's invasion.
positions.quote: I will stand firmly with our allies, including Israel as it combats terrorism, and Ukraine as it defends itself against Russia’s illegal invasion.

positions.summary: Focuses on preserving Social Security and Medicare for current retirees through spending oversight rather than expanding public coverage; does not call for expanded public health coverage.

summary.text: Alan Bond is an independent candidate running on the Hope for Tomorrow Party line for New Jersey's 11th Congressional District. He holds degrees from Dartmouth College and Harvard Business School and previously worked in pension-fund management, a career that ended in a 2002 federal fraud conviction and a prison term. He also ran in and lost the April 2026 special election for this seat.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Dartmouth College and a graduate degree from Harvard Business School; worked in business strategy and as a pension-fund manager.
Ran as an independent in the April 16, 2026 special election for NJ-11 and received 0.5% of the vote.

priorities.text: Supporting small businesses and job creation through investment in infrastructure, workforce development, and technology.
Expanding access to quality education from early childhood through college and career pathways.
Making healthcare more accessible and affordable, including lower prescription drug costs and expanded mental-health services.

positions.summary: Supports policies that expand access to quality healthcare, reduce prescription drug costs, and ensure mental-health services are available to all who need them.
Supports climate action and expanding renewable-energy and green jobs while supporting sustainable economic growth.

record.text: Indicted in December 1999 for a pension-fund "kickback" scheme that diverted $6.9 million to personal accounts, and again in August 2001 for a securities "cherry picking" scheme; pleaded guilty to the kickback scheme, was convicted by a federal jury on six counts of fraud in the cherry-picking case on June 10, 2002, and was sentenced in 2003 to 12 years and 7 months in prison and ordered to pay $6.6 million in restitution. He was released from prison in 2008.

summary.text: Vincent Matrisciano is a write-in candidate on the Common Sense Independent Party line for New Jersey's 11th Congressional District. He has worked in public service; no detailed biography, platform, or campaign statements were available.

background.text: Career experience includes working in public service.

researchNotes: Analilia Mejia has not yet completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, so her positions above are drawn from her campaign website's issues page rather than a direct Q&A; her committee assignments in the 119th Congress could not be confirmed because congress.gov and govtrack.us were unreachable in this environment (added separately if available). Joe Hathaway's positions are likewise drawn from his campaign platform page rather than a completed survey. Alan Bond's platform page had limited detail beyond broad issue headings. Vincent Matrisciano, a certified write-in candidate, has essentially no public campaign footprint beyond a one-line Ballotpedia biography; researched at minimal depth as instructed for candidates with little footprint.
